hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan ROM Controller (`rom_ctrl`) performs a boot-time integrity check by reading ROM words in order and presenting them to KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code). The affected functionality is the `rom_ctrl_counter` / ROM-address generation path that drives `rom_addr_o` for this ROM-to-KMAC stream.

## Expected Behavior
When a ROM word is already valid and KMAC accepts it by asserting ready, `rom_addr_o` must advance to the next sequential ROM word in that same cycle so the next ROM fetch starts immediately. In particular, if the first pending word is at address 0 and KMAC changes from not ready to ready, `rom_addr_o` must become 1 immediately rather than remaining at 0 for an extra cycle.

## Actual Behavior
After KMAC applies back-pressure and then becomes ready again, the ROM Controller keeps `rom_addr_o` on the previous address for one extra cycle. In the reset-start case, address 0 is presented for an extra cycle when KMAC first accepts data, so the first ROM word is fetched twice instead of the read stream advancing immediately to the next word.

## Trigger Condition
This bug is triggered while `rom_ctrl` is streaming ROM contents to KMAC and KMAC temporarily deasserts ready while a valid ROM word is pending, then reasserts ready. A concrete edge case is immediately after reset release: the first ROM word is pending at address 0, KMAC is initially not ready, and then KMAC asserts ready.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Advance the ROM address once for each valid/ready word handshake, including the first handshake after a stall.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: After KMAC released backpressure, the ROM stream address remained on the accepted word for one extra cycle and fetched it twice.

hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
`prim_packer` is an OpenTitan primitive that packs masked input data into fixed-width output words and connects them with valid/ready handshakes on both its input and output sides. Its backpressure handling is incorrect when a single accepted input transfer already fills one complete output word while the downstream side is stalled.

## Expected Behavior
If an accepted input transfer causes `prim_packer` to buffer at least one complete `OutW`-bit output word, `valid_o` must assert and remain asserted until the downstream side accepts that word with `ready_i`. While that full output word is pending and `ready_i` is low, `ready_o` must deassert so the upstream side cannot send another input transfer, unless the pending output word is accepted in the same cycle.

This must also hold when one input transfer alone provides the full output word, for example when `InW == OutW` and `mask_i` selects the entire input word.

## Actual Behavior
In the current implementation, when `ready_i` is low and one accepted input transfer already provides a full output word, `prim_packer` can behave as though no complete output word is pending on the following cycle. `valid_o` can drop even though a complete output word is already buffered, and `ready_o` can remain asserted instead of applying backpressure.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the downstream interface is stalled (`ready_i` low) at the same time that an accepted input transfer makes the buffered data reach or exceed one full `OutW`-bit output word. A minimal case is `InW == OutW`, `valid_i` asserted for one input transfer, `mask_i` all ones, and `ready_i` held low until the pending output word is accepted.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the `prim_packer` primitive's output-valid generation and upstream-ready/backpressure behavior when a complete packed output word has been buffered but has not yet been acknowledged by the downstream interface.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Treat an all-masked input as one complete buffered word. Hold the word and apply upstream backpressure until it is accepted.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: A full packed word could stop appearing valid and upstream ready could remain asserted when the downstream interface was stalled.

hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in OpenTitan's `prim_arbiter` primitive. If one requester has already been selected but the downstream interface keeps `arb_ready` low, a later higher-priority requester can replace the first requester before any `arb_valid && arb_ready` handshake occurs. This changes the granted requester and `arb_data` for a transfer that is still pending. The problem can appear on TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) request paths such as `tlul_socket_m1`, where the downstream side may observe request information change without a new handshake.

## Expected Behavior
After `prim_arbiter` raises `arb_valid` for a requester, that same requester and its associated `arb_data` must remain selected until the transfer is accepted with `arb_valid && arb_ready`. If another requester asserts later while the first transfer is stalled, it must wait for the next arbitration opportunity. On TL-UL paths, this means request fields carried through the arbiter, such as address or write data, must not change while `valid` remains asserted and `ready` is low.

## Actual Behavior
While a transfer is stalled by `arb_ready == 0`, asserting a later higher-priority request can change the arbiter output before the original transfer is accepted. The pending transfer can therefore appear to switch to the newer request, changing the observed grant and forwarded data without an acceptance handshake.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is `prim_arbiter`'s handling of a request that has already been selected but has not yet been accepted.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when a requester is selected, `arb_valid` remains high, the downstream interface applies backpressure with `arb_ready == 0`, and another requester with higher priority becomes active before the stalled transfer is accepted.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Select the highest active requester when idle, then hold the one-hot grant and selected data until ack_i.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: A later higher-priority request could replace the requester and data of an already-selected transfer before acknowledgement.

hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
The Entropy Distribution Network (EDN) hardware-controlled command path to the Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator (CSRNG) can violate the CSRNG command valid/ready protocol when CSRNG reports an acknowledge/status error while an EDN hardware command is already pending. The affected logic is the EDN path that issues hardware-controlled CSRNG commands, including the boot request mode sequence.

## Expected Behavior
After EDN asserts the CSRNG command-valid signal for a hardware command, it must keep that request asserted until CSRNG raises the corresponding ready signal and the valid/ready handshake completes. If CSRNG reports an acknowledge/status error before that handshake completes, EDN must still finish the outstanding handshake first. Only after the handshake is complete should EDN record the CSRNG acknowledge error, raise its recovery status, and move into its reject/error state.

## Actual Behavior
If CSRNG signals an acknowledge/status error while the request is stalled and CSRNG is still not ready, EDN can drop the command-valid signal immediately. This cancels the in-flight hardware command before the handshake completes and violates the EDN-to-CSRNG valid/ready protocol.

## Trigger Conditions
This happens when EDN is issuing a hardware-controlled CSRNG command, CSRNG is backpressuring the interface so the request is waiting with valid high and ready low, and a CSRNG acknowledge/status error is reported during that stall. A representative case is boot request mode, where EDN has started a boot-time instantiate or generate command and CSRNG is not yet ready to accept it.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Hold command valid and payload until ready completes the handshake. An error may be recorded but cannot cancel the in-flight command.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: An acknowledge-status error could cancel a pending CSRNG command while the receiver was still applying backpressure.

hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
CVA6's memory management unit (MMU) reports load/store misaligned exceptions on a one-cycle-delayed interface to the load/store unit (LSU). The LSU consumes the MMU response one cycle after the request phase, but the misaligned-exception state is not kept with the originating request across that delay. As a result, the exception seen with an LSU response can come from the wrong request cycle instead of the memory access that actually faulted.

## Expected Behavior
For RISC-V load and store address-misaligned faults, the exception reported by the MMU-to-LSU response path must belong to the same memory access that caused it. A response for a misaligned access should appear on the following LSU response cycle with the correct misaligned exception, and a cycle with no pending LSU response must not expose a leftover misaligned exception.

## Actual Behavior
The MMU can present a misaligned exception from the wrong cycle. This can misattribute the exception to a different load/store response, and in the boundary case where the original misaligned access is followed by a cycle with no LSU request, a stale misaligned exception can still remain visible.

## Affected Function
The MMU-to-LSU load/store response path for misaligned-access exception reporting.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when a misaligned load or store enters the MMU and the corresponding LSU response is consumed one cycle later. If the next cycle does not match the original request context, especially when there is no new LSU request, the misaligned exception can be reported on the wrong cycle or leak into the idle cycle.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Pipeline request validity and its misaligned flag together so the response exception belongs to the originating access.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: A one-cycle-delayed MMU response could use the misalignment state from the wrong request cycle or leak it into an idle cycle.

hwe_bench.problem_statement:
The OpenTitan always-on timer (AON timer) wakeup request path does not satisfy the power manager (`pwrmgr`) wakeup protocol. The power manager does not latch incoming wakeup requests, so each wakeup source must hold its wakeup output high until software acknowledges the event by clearing that source's recorded wakeup cause.

For the AON timer, when its wakeup threshold expires while sleep mode is active, the timer records the wakeup cause and asserts its wakeup request. If the system then exits sleep because of that wakeup before software clears the AON timer wakeup cause register (`WKUP_CAUSE`), the wakeup request must remain asserted. It should deassert only after software clears `WKUP_CAUSE`. The observed bug is that the AON timer wakeup request can drop as soon as sleep mode is exited, even though the wakeup cause is still set and software has not acknowledged it.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Latch each wakeup_event_i and keep wakeup_o asserted until clear_cause_i, independent of the current sleeping_i value.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: A timer wakeup request could drop when sleep ended even though software had not cleared the recorded wakeup cause.

## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan ENTROPY_SRC (Entropy Source) IP's hardware-conditioned FIPS seed generation path, specifically the handoff from the health-test completion logic to the SHA3 conditioner when `RNG_BIT_ENABLE` selects a single RNG lane. The affected logic is the ENTROPY_SRC main state machine and SHA3 conditioning interface that convert health-tested raw entropy into a conditioned seed output in single-lane FIPS operation.

## Expected Behavior
When ENTROPY_SRC is generating hardware-conditioned FIPS seeds from a single RNG lane, SHA3 must not start processing until every word belonging to the completed health-test window has been accepted from the pre-conditioner FIFO. In single-lane mode, the health-test completion pulse can arrive one cycle too early. This causes SHA3 `process_i` to assert before the last word from the pre-conditioner FIFO has been absorbed. ## Trigger Condition
The failure occurs when ENTROPY_SRC is configured for FIPS hardware conditioning with `RNG_BIT_ENABLE` selecting one of the four RNG lanes, and a health-test window completes while the final pre-conditioner FIFO word for that window is still being handed to SHA3. hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
CVA6 reports illegal-instruction exceptions from its CVXIF custom-instruction interface through the `x_exception_o` record produced by `cvxif_fu`. When the RISC-V hypervisor extension (RVH) is enabled, the illegal-instruction path does not fully initialize the hypervisor-specific fields of that record. Trap handling can then consume undefined metadata, and `mtinst` (the machine-trap transformed-instruction CSR) may capture arbitrary values instead of deterministic exception state.

## Expected Behavior
For a CVXIF-generated illegal-instruction exception, the exception record must be fully defined before trap CSRs consume it. The cause must remain illegal instruction, the rejected instruction value in `tval` must stay correct when that field is enabled, hypervisor-only payload fields that have no meaningful value on this path must be zero, and the guest-virtual-address flag must match the current virtualization state rather than an undefined or stale value.

## Actual Behavior
With RVH enabled, the illegal-instruction path can leave hypervisor-specific metadata in `x_exception_o` undriven. This makes transformed-instruction metadata non-deterministic and can corrupt `mtinst`; other hypervisor exception fields may also depend on arbitrary logic state.

## Affected Function
The CVXIF exception-generation logic in `cvxif_fu`, specifically the illegal-instruction exception record emitted on `x_exception_o`.

hwe_bench.problem_statement:
The Access Control Range Check (`ac_range_check`) IP filters TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) requests against configured address ranges and permissions. If a request matches multiple enabled ranges, the lowest-index matching range has priority and is supposed to determine whether that specific access type is allowed.

The current RTL can violate that priority rule when overlapping enabled ranges disagree on permissions by access type. In particular, a higher-priority range that denies reads but allows writes can be overridden by a lower-priority overlapping range that allows reads but denies writes, causing a read request that hits both ranges to be forwarded even though the higher-priority range should block it.

Expected behavior is that `ac_range_check` resolves permissions per requested access type using the highest-priority matching range. In the overlapping-range scenario above, the read must be denied: the filtered TL-UL request must not be forwarded, the module must generate its deny response, and, when deny logging is enabled, `LOG_STATUS.deny_range_index` must report the index of the range that actually caused the deny. The same overlap must still allow the write request, because the highest-priority matching range permits writes.

Trigger condition: at least two enabled `ac_range_check` ranges overlap on the same address, the lower-index range has higher priority, and the overlapping ranges grant different access types for that address. The bug is visible when a request uses an access type that the highest-priority matching range denies but a lower-priority matching range allows.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Choose the first enabled matching range, index 0 before index 1. Use only that range's read or write permission for the requested access type.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: An overlapping lower-priority access-control range could override the per-access permission of the lower-index winning range.

upstream.title: [ac_range_check/rtl] Fix permission checking and deny index

derivation: standalone real-fix-derived reduction; not a full upstream regression

hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
`prim_fifo_sync` is OpenTitan's synchronous first-in, first-out (FIFO) primitive. When an instance becomes empty after its last queued element is read, the primitive can still expose that old element on its read-data output. This behavior is externally visible in downstream users such as the UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) receive FIFO, but the underlying bug is in `prim_fifo_sync` itself.

## Expected Behavior
When a `prim_fifo_sync` instance has no valid entry available, its read interface should represent the empty state unambiguously: `rvalid_o` must be low, and `rdata_o` must be `0` rather than the value of the most recently dequeued entry. This must still hold for a one-entry FIFO configuration after its only queued byte has been read.

## Actual Behavior
After the final queued entry is dequeued, `rvalid_o` drops as expected, but `rdata_o` continues to drive the previous value instead of returning to `0`. As a result, software or logic that samples the read-data output while the FIFO is empty can observe stale data from the last entry.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the empty-state read-output behavior of the `prim_fifo_sync` primitive, including instances used on software-visible receive paths such as the UART receive FIFO.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered by writing at least one element into a `prim_fifo_sync` instance, reading until the FIFO becomes empty, and then observing the read interface before any new write occurs. The benchmarked boundary case includes a single-entry FIFO that is written once and then read once.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Implement a one-entry FIFO. When empty, valid_o is zero and data_o is zero; when full, data_o is the stored byte until it is read.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: A one-entry FIFO correctly dropped valid after its last read but continued to expose the stale dequeued byte on its data output.

upstream.title: [prim_fifo_sync] Make FIFO output zero when empty
